questions.q: Find the radius of convergence of $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{x^n}{n}$.
questions.answer: Ratio test: $\left|\frac{x^{n+1}/(n+1)}{x^n/n}\right| \to |x|$. Converges for $|x|<1$: radius of convergence $R=1$.

questions.q: Find the radius of convergence of $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^n}{n!}$.
questions.answer: Ratio test: $\left|\frac{x^{n+1}n!}{(n+1)!x^n}\right| = \frac{|x|}{n+1} \to 0$ for every $x$: radius of convergence $R=\infty$.

questions.q: Find the first three nonzero terms of the Maclaurin series for $f(x) = e^x$, using $f^{(n)}(0) = 1$ for all $n$.
Find the third-degree Taylor polynomial for $f(x) = \cos x$ centered at $x = 0$.
Use the Maclaurin series $\sin x = x - \frac{x^3}{6} + \frac{x^5}{120} - \cdots$ to approximate $\sin(0.2)$ using the first two nonzero terms, to four decimal places.
Find the interval of convergence of $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x-2)^n}{n}$, checking both endpoints.
questions.answer: Ratio test gives radius $R=1$, centered at $x=2$: $1<x<3$ tentatively. At $x=3$: $\sum\frac{1}{n}$ diverges (harmonic). At $x=1$: $\sum\frac{(-1)^n}{n}$ converges (alternating). Interval of convergence: $[1,3)$.

questions.q: Find the radius of convergence of $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n!\,x^n$.
questions.answer: Ratio test: $\left|\frac{(n+1)!x^{n+1}}{n!x^n}\right| = (n+1)|x| \to \infty$ for any $x\neq0$. The series converges only at $x=0$: radius of convergence $R=0$.

questions.q: Using the known Maclaurin series $e^x = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}$, write the Maclaurin series for $e^{-x^2}$ (substitute $-x^2$ for $x$), giving the first three terms.
Using $\frac{1}{1-x}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}x^n$ for $|x|<1$, write the power series for $\frac{1}{1+x^2}$ (substitute $-x^2$ for $x$).

sections.heading: Taylor series centered at a nonzero point

questions.q: Find the first three terms of the Taylor series for $f(x)=\ln x$ centered at $x=1$, using $f(1)=0$, $f'(1)=1$, $f''(1)=-1$.
Find the second-degree Taylor polynomial for $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ centered at $x=4$, given $f(4)=2$, $f'(4)=\frac{1}{4}$, $f''(4)=-\frac{1}{32}$.
Using the second-degree Maclaurin polynomial for $\cos x$, $T_2(x)=1-\frac{x^2}{2}$, estimate $\cos(0.3)$ to four decimal places, and compare to the true value $\cos(0.3)\approx0.9553$.
questions.answer: $T_2(0.3) = 1 - \frac{0.09}{2} = 1-0.045 = 0.9550$, very close to the true value $0.9553$ (error $\approx0.0003$).
